summary.title: The Most Important Coding Habits
summary.one_liner: Healthy daily habits, such as stretching, regular breaks, avoiding late-night coding, and improving your desk setup, help programmers avoid back pain and keep coding for years.
takeaways: Long hours hunched over a keyboard can weaken supporting muscles and strain the back, which can lead to a slipped disc.
Daily central and lower body stretches help keep muscles supple and able to support the spine.
Take a short non-screen break at least once an hour; breaks can also help solve coding problems.
Avoid coding when exhausted, and set a firm time to stop working each day.
A laptop stand, ergonomic chair, or standing desk can improve comfort and encourage movement.
summary.summary: The author, recovering from a slipped disc attributed to years of poor posture while coding, presents a set of personal habits to protect the body. The advice covers daily stretching, taking hourly breaks, not coding late at night when tired, and improving the workspace with a laptop stand, ergonomic chair, or standing desk. It is a first-person, experience-based blog post rather than a technical guide, with no code or formal study cited.
